Compare numbers of topics and segmentation levels

Source: R/compare.R
compare_topics.Rd

compare_topics() fits topics() for every candidate number of topics, and for every segmentation level in segment, on one shared set of embeddings, and reports measures of the quality of each fit. The number of topics, like the unit of analysis (the whole document or its sentences, clauses, or phrases), sets the granularity of a topic model and has no single correct value: fewer topics give broad themes, more topics give narrower ones, until some of them split a theme into near-duplicates.

Three measures are reported per candidate: the mean coherence of the topics' terms (coherence()), the diversity of the terms across topics (topic_diversity()), and the share of the embedding variance that lies between topics. Coherence tends to fall and between-topic variance to rise as the number of topics grows, so a useful candidate is often the count after which coherence stops improving rather than the count with the highest coherence. Comparing candidates on such measures is a better basis for the choice than fixing a number in advance. The function compares; it does not choose.

The result is a table of class sbert_topic_sweep with one row per candidate. The fitted candidates are kept, so a chosen one is taken out with fitted() without refitting.

The measures are a guide; the choice should also rest on reading the representative texts of the candidate models.

Usage

compare_topics(
  text,
  n_topics = c(5L, 10L, 15L, 20L, 25L, 30L),
  column = NULL,
  model = NULL,
  embeddings = NULL,
  measure = c("npmi", "umass"),
  n_terms = 10L,
  n_representatives = 1L,
  keep_models = TRUE,
  batch_size = 32L,
  cores = 1L,
  segment = c("document", "sentence", "clause", "phrase"),
  max_tokens = NULL,
  merge_below = 0L,
  min_content = 0,
  coherence_weight = c("none", "size"),
  ...
)

Arguments

text

Documents: a character vector, a data frame together with column, or a corpus prepared by topic_corpus().

n_topics

Candidate numbers of topics: distinct integers of at least 2 and below the number of modeled units. Default c(5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30).

column

Name of the text column when text is a data frame. The other columns are carried into the document table. Rows whose text is missing, blank, or the placeholder "[No abstract available]" are dropped, and so are their rows of embeddings. NULL (default) for a character vector.

model

The encoder: a model from load_model(), a pinned model name, or NULL (default) for the default model. Not used when embeddings are given.

embeddings

Optional precomputed embedding matrix, one row per modeled unit. When several segment levels are compared, a list of matrices named by level. Default NULL.

measure

Coherence measure: "npmi" (default) or "umass".

n_terms

Top terms per topic used for coherence and diversity (default 10).

n_representatives

Representative units stored per topic in each candidate (default 1).

keep_models

Whether to keep the fitted candidates (default TRUE). With FALSE, only the table is kept and fitted() is not available.

batch_size

Texts encoded per model call (default 32).

cores

Number of forked worker processes for tokenization and for fitting the candidates (default 1; Unix-alikes only). Results do not depend on it.

segment

Unit or units of analysis, as in topics(): one or more of "document" (default), "sentence", "clause", and "phrase". With several levels, every level is fitted for every candidate.

max_tokens, merge_below, min_content

Segmentation options passed to segment(), for segmented fits only: the maximum segment length (in the model's tokens, or in words with precomputed embeddings; default NULL, no limit), the number of words below which a segment is joined to its neighbor (default 0), and the minimum share of letters for a segment to be kept (default 0; see content_ratio()).

coherence_weight

How the coherences of a candidate's topics are averaged: "none" (default), every topic equally, or "size", each topic in proportion to its number of units, so a very small topic cannot decide the comparison.

...

Further arguments to topics(), for example stop_words or weighting.

Value

An object of class sbert_topic_sweep: a data frame with one row per candidate and columns n_topics, coherence (the mean over the topics that can be scored, averaged as coherence_weight says; NA when no topic can be scored), topic_diversity, explained (the between-topic share of the variance), and converged, preceded by segment when several levels are compared. The coherence measure and the weighting are kept as the attributes measure and coherence_weight. summary() gives the most coherent candidate per level, plot() draws the measures, and fitted() returns a fitted candidate.

Conditions

Errors of class sbert_bad_input when fewer than three units are modeled, a candidate is not below the number of units, a list of embeddings is given for a single level, several levels are given with a prepared corpus or with embeddings that are not a list named by level; and the conditions of topics() for each candidate. Non-convergence of a candidate is recorded in the converged column.

See also

topics() to fit one model; coherence() and topic_diversity() for the measures; topic_hierarchy() and reduce_topics() to merge the topics of a fit.

Examples

corpus <- head(dedupe(feedback_translations, column = "translation"), 600)
comparison <- compare_topics(corpus, n_topics = c(4, 6, 8),
                             column = "translation",
                             embeddings = feedback_embeddings)
comparison
#> <sbert_topic_sweep> 3 candidates, coherence measure: npmi
#>  n_topics  coherence topic_diversity explained converged
#>         4 -0.2070855       0.9250000 0.1229819      TRUE
#>         6 -0.1044246       0.9166667 0.2255144      TRUE
#>         8 -0.1181287       0.9000000 0.2433832      TRUE
#> 
#> Fitted models retained: fitted(x, n_topics = 6)
summary(comparison)
#> Topic-count comparison: highest mean npmi coherence per level
#> 
#>   segment n_candidates min_topics max_topics best_n_topics coherence
#>  document            3          4          8             6    -0.104
#>  topic_diversity explained all_converged
#>            0.917     0.226          TRUE
fitted(comparison, n_topics = 6)
#> <sbert_topic_model>
#>   documents: 600 
#>   topics: 6
#>   model: precomputed embeddings
#>   algorithm: deterministic k-means (Lloyd)
#>   topic sizes: 223, 133, 131, 49, 37, 27
#>   between/total SS: 22.6%

# Documents against sentences (one embedding matrix per level)
documents <- c(
  "Cats chase mice. Stocks and bonds trade.",
  "Dogs chase balls. Markets price shares.",
  "Kittens nap in sunshine. Banks report profit."
)
levels <- compare_topics(
  documents,
  n_topics = 2,
  segment = c("document", "sentence"),
  embeddings = list(
    document = rbind(c(0.7, 0.7), c(0.6, 0.8), c(0.8, 0.6)),
    sentence = rbind(
      c(1, 0), c(0, 1), c(0.9, 0.1),
      c(0.1, 0.9), c(0.95, 0.05), c(0.05, 0.95)
    )
  ),
  n_terms = 2
)
levels
#> <sbert_topic_sweep> 2 candidates, coherence measure: npmi
#>   segment n_topics  coherence topic_diversity explained converged
#>  document        2  0.6845351               1 0.7491596      TRUE
#>  sentence        2 -0.1934264               1 0.9954323      TRUE
#> 
#> Fitted models retained: fitted(x, n_topics = 2, segment = "document")
